newsitem.title: MEXICO: Gruma leaders hail ADM deal.
newsitem.headline: Gruma leaders hail ADM deal.

text.p: Mexico's Gruma SA de CV gained greatly from last year's link up with U.S. agribusiness giant Archer Daniels Midland Co, Gruma directors told shareholders on Monday. Last September, Gruma sold a 22 percent stake to ADM for $258 million and the two companies began a corn-flour joint venture in the United States administered by its unit Grupo Industrial Maseca SA de CV.
A Gruma statement did not give any figures illustrating how the deal with ADM had improved Gruma's balance sheet.

But the ADM-Maseca deal matched two of the biggest food companies in the United States and Mexico, and gave Gruma a higher profile in the growing U.S. corn-flour and tortilla market. It also eliminated ADM as a competitor.
The deal with ADM was one of the highlights of an address by director general Eduardo Livas to shareholders, Gruma said.
Gruma boosted its corn-flour production by 400 million tonnes in 1996 through new production lines in existing plants, increasing the operating margin to 8.2 percent in 1996 from 7.2 percent in 1995.
"It's worth mentioning that continuing with its expansion strategy, Gruma invested $104 million in 1996 to modernize the infrastructure of plants built in recent years," the statement said.
Gruma had sales of 11.738 billion pesos in 1996, of which 46 percent came from operations outside Mexico, the company said. Sales were up 20 percent over 1995.
Livas told a news conference after the meeting that Gruma and Maseca would announce their first-quarter results on Thursday or Friday.
